contexts.text: The falsities wherewith the good, which is Moab, is defiled, are here called lees (), in which the taste and odour remain, if he is not reformed.
Those who are defiled with earthly dregs are in the region of the intestines...
All evil is contagious, and pollutes, as lees do dough...
Then what is false falls down, like lees; and the truth comes forth purified; like wine, which is clarified after fermentation, when the lees are falling to the bottom. DP 284:2.
The conjugial external... is (then) purified from its lees by the internal...
Cupidities are like lees, which precipitate themselves to the bottom, when the must of the wine is being clarified.
The body absorbs (the internal affections), and involves them in its lees.
The feculent delights of scortatory love...
He had been saturated with the same dregs.
(The skin and its coats) exhale more subtle faeces...
A feast of lees, or of the best wine () = the appropriation of truths.
The dregs of the cup () = mere falsities from which are evils.
Its dregs they shall suck out (). Explained ( = the penalty of profanation. AE 1116.)
Like the effervescence from lees, which is concupiscence.
By lees, defecated lees () are signified the truths from that good, with the happiness from them.
3. The feculent blood of the heart is purified in the lungs.
